Hengshuang Zhao老师实验室.debug_abstract: Visual control maps visual streams to actions in reinforcement learning and vision-language-action (VLA) policies. Changing weather, noise, blur, and compression can obscure different task cues within one episode. Existing control benchmarks mainly test scene distractions, while generic restorers optimize whole-image fidelity. We introduce the Visual Degraded Control Suite (VDCS) to evaluate seven degradations under Markov switching. We propose Agent-Centric Observations with Mixture-of-Experts (ACO-MoE), which routes each frame to a repair expert, restores RGB content, and composes task-relevant foregrounds. On eight VDCS tasks, corruption lowers DreamerV3's mean return from 769 to 562. ACO-MoE raises it to 730, recovering 81.2% of the lost return. It also improves returns on DMC-GB and RoboSuite and retains 70% to 97% of clean-input mean return under six unseen perturbation families. We train ACO-MoE on robot demonstrations and deploy it with a 3B-parameter VLA policy on a Piper arm for cube placement in blue and white boxes and cup placement on a coaster. On the blue-box and cup tasks, motion blur and physical low light with added noise reduce success from 100% to at most 10%. ACO-MoE raises success to 75% to 95% over 20 trials per task and condition.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: Outcome-Balanced PPO and Policy-Induced Flow Rectification for Flow-Based VLA Policies
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Yuhan Wang, Ruiyang Wang, Jiaguan Zhu
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: The paper presents an RL framework combining Outcome-Balanced PPO and flow rectification to enhance flow-based VLA policies, improving task success rates in simulations.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables post-training of flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) policies by optimizing expected task return through environment interaction. However, this optimization raises two challenges: policy updates can alter the velocity-field geometry underlying the score approximation used for stochastic transitions, and sparse multi-task rollouts can yield uneven learning signals across tasks and advantage signs. We introduce an RL framework that combines Outcome-Balanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with policy-induced flow rectification. Outcome-Balanced PPO reweights positive advantages using task success-rate estimates and rescales positive and negative advantages while preserving their signs. Policy-induced rectification periodically fits a linear-bridge flow to ODE endpoint pairs generated by the current policy, refreshing the representation used in subsequent stochastic optimization. We evaluate the framework on simulated manipulation benchmarks and additionally study a component combination in a Real2Sim2Real task, examining task performance, optimization behavior, and flow consistency. The proposed framework improves success rates over the evaluated baselines across the simulated benchmarks.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: PACT: Plan-Action Consistency Training by Preserving Correct Plans and Repairing Actions in GUI Agents
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Zhuohan Cai, Zhangxuan Gu, Runze Li, Beitong Zhou, Ming Wen
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: PACT is a training framework that enhances GUI agents' task success by aligning plans with actions, reducing execution gaps, and improving overall performance across platforms.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: GUI agents can formulate a correct immediate plan in their reasoning yet emit an action that fails to execute it, creating an execution gap. This recurring mismatch undermines reliable task completion, as a single execution error can derail a multi-step workflow. In outcome-supervised reinforcement learning, broadcasting a negative response-level advantage across all generated tokens risks penalizing valid planning together with erroneous execution. To address this credit-assignment conflict, we introduce PACT (Plan-Action Consistency Training), a training framework that combines reference-aligned plan protection and plan-aligned action repair without altering the original scalar action reward. Using annotated reference actions to identify execution gaps, PACT protects the verified plan by masking negative policy-gradient contributions across its token span. Keeping the generated reasoning unchanged as context, it then favors the reference action over the emitted erroneous action through a preference surrogate with stop-gradient pair weights. Compared with the outcome-only baseline, PACT raises AndroidWorld task success from 60.34% to 68.97% (+8.63 pp), while improving rule-based plan-action consistency on AndroidControl High from 83.71% to 89.74% (+6.03 pp). Adapting PACT to desktop agents also improves task success from 40.92% to 44.17% (+3.25 pp) on the full 369-task OSWorld benchmark. Together, these results establish PACT as an effective credit-assignment framework for bridging execution gaps and improving task completion across mobile and desktop GUI environments.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: Encoding, Decodability, and Use: A Five-Layer Framework for Benchmark Measurement Audits with Evidence from UAV Intent Recognition
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: This paper introduces a five-layer framework for evaluating UAV intent recognition, revealing significant limitations in model understanding and measurement accuracy across various layers.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Benchmark accuracy is routinely read as evidence that a model understands the construct the benchmark measures. We propose and instantiate on AeroIntent a five-layer framework that decomposes that reading into observation, representation, decoding, use, and behaviour. The framework separates encoding, decodability, and use as distinct levels. In the instantiation, the observation layer is unreliable on 7 of the 20 Drone programs and floors the direct visual correlate of radial velocity at a 0.26\% scale change. The representation layer exposes two task-designed RGB features with nominal signals. RAFT flow radial bias reaches $r=+0.257$ ($p=0.030$), and bounding-box optical-flow divergence reaches $r=+0.203$ ($p=0.029$). No multi-feature readout gives a fold-mean test correlation above the cluster minimum detectable effect (MDE), and the largest positive global out-of-sample correlation is $r=+0.080$. The decoding layer sets the MDE at $|r|=0.599$ at the multi-feature Bonferroni threshold ($α=0.00714$, power 0.80), and the observed $r=+0.080$ has power 0.00. Two injection experiments establish the MDE's condition from both sides: aligned injections are detected at or above the simulated power, and orthogonal injections are not detected. The use layer finds accuracy consistent with program memory (program-identity 0.937/0.597/0.210) and multi-region static cues. The behaviour layer is consistent with accuracy not requiring a radial-velocity readout (appearance 0.6552 vs bounding-box trajectory 0.4080, cluster-level paired $Δ=+0.2471$, $p=0.0132$).

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: DuoFlow: Towards Synchronized Speech and Motion Generation with Fine-Grained Control
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Jun Dong, Ronghui Li, Zhongyuan Hu, Yunqi Zhao, Lijie Guo
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: DuoFlow introduces a dual-stream transformer for synchronized speech and motion generation, enabling fine-grained control over vocal style and body movement through structured conditions.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: An embodied speaker's expressiveness depends not only on what is said, but also on how the voice sounds and how the body moves. However, existing joint speech-motion generation models are largely driven implicitly by transcript semantics or intermediate speech representations, offering little explicit control over motion hierarchy, body parts, or vocal style. To bridge this gap, we construct MotionSpeech, a structured benchmark for controllable joint speech-motion generation that includes transcripts, voice-style descriptions, and motion conditions at two hierarchical levels. Building on this benchmark, we propose DuoFlow, a dual-stream latent flow transformer that jointly denoises speech and motion under a shared noise level and a unified second-based temporal coordinate. Modality-specific residual connectors inject structured conditions into the corresponding streams, layer-wise bidirectional cross-modal attention coordinates their generation, and a monotonic phoneme pathway combines normalized progress anchors with CTC supervision to strengthen speech temporal modeling. DuoFlow provides a unified interface for fine-grained motion and vocal-style control and demonstrates the ability to synthesize high-quality, synchronized, and instruction-consistent speech-motion sequences. Project page, https://jundong-dev.github.io/DuoFlow-project-page.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: SkillEarth: Teaching General-Purpose Agents to Act on Earth via Skill Evolution
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Haojun Tang, Wenda Zhao, Xiang Zhou, Qiwei Lin, Lida Huang
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: SkillEarth introduces a self-evolving skill extraction method for remote sensing agents, enabling adaptable, reusable skills through observation-grounded evolution without expert intervention or retraining.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Recently developed remote sensing (RS) agents execute real-world tasks with complex workflows through multi-step tool invocation. These agents, however, typically rely on predefined expertise or parameter updates. They thus require updating expert knowledge or retraining models whenever new tools, tasks, or execution patterns emerge, limiting their continual adaptability in dynamic Earth environments. In this work, we seek to equip general-purpose agents with RS tool-call knowledge that can be automatically extracted from demonstrated trajectories without expert intervention or parameter updates. Specifically, we propose SkillEarth, a self-evolving skill extraction method that externalizes RS tool-call knowledge as reusable, retrievable, and evolvable skill files and refines them through observation-grounded evolution. Unlike existing automatic skill extraction methods that rely on outcome-based reflection to refine skills holistically, SkillEarth grounds skill evolution in real tool-chain execution and combines dual-judge feedback with a grounded observation routing graph for precise component-level refinement. The resulting skills are generalizable, reliable, and transferable: they improve overall RS tool-call performance across three frontier LLMs and four open-source LLMs, are refined through real tool execution feedback, and support cross-model reuse without retraining. Experiments on OpenEarth-Bench and Earth-Bench demonstrate that SkillEarth achieves better tool selection, argument correctness, execution-order consistency, and task completion than existing RS agents and skill extraction methods.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: TouchBridge: Tactile-Conditioned Human-to-Robot Transfer for Dexterous Manipulation
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Haozhe Zhang, Gu Zhang, Zirui Zou, Yuzheng Chen, Jinlong Wu
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: TouchBridge enables efficient human-to-robot transfer of dexterous manipulation skills through a tactile-conditioned framework, achieving high success rates with faster demonstration collection.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Human demonstrations offer an efficient and scalable source of data for dexterous robot manipulation, but differences in sensing and hand morphology complicate the transfer of contact-rich interactions. We present TouchBridge, a hardware--software co-designed framework for human-to-robot data transformation. A wearable human demonstration interface and a corresponding robot interface establish cross-embodiment correspondence in visual and fingertip tactile sensing. We introduce Tac-Retarget, a tactile-conditioned retargeting method that uses measured contact to align fingertip contact patches and preserve their spatial relations within and across hands. Unlike object-aware or simulation-based transfer pipelines, Tac-Retarget requires no object mesh, object-pose estimate, or physics simulation for retargeting, enabling direct and scalable conversion of human demonstrations into robot-domain training data. Combined with visual synthesis and camera-anchored action conversion, TouchBridge produces robot-domain demonstrations for fine-tuning a pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) model. Across four real-world contact-rich tasks, policies fine-tuned solely on TouchBridge-converted human demonstrations achieve a 72.5% average success rate, compared with 77.5% using an equal number of teleoperated robot demonstrations, while human demonstration collection is 7.0x faster. Under the same policy and training setup, Tac-Retarget outperforms DexPilot and UniDex by 25.0 and 42.5 percentage points, respectively.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: RIPPLE: Recovery Internalization through Process-Level Policy Learning and Effect-Aware Credit for Long-Horizon Agentic Coding
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Jingxuan Xu, Zihang Xu, Yuechen Luo, Ziqi Miao, Wenqiang Zhu
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: RIPPLE is a training framework that enhances long-horizon coding agents' recovery capabilities by integrating process-level guidance and stage-specific credit assignment for improved decision-making.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Long-horizon coding agents can observe a failure and generate a plausible critique yet continue along the same incorrect trajectory. We call this the Critique-to-Action Handoff Gap. We introduce RIPPLE, a recovery-oriented training framework that internalizes process-level guidance into a single self-recovering policy. A prefix-only teacher provides evidence-grounded recovery supervision without access to future actions or terminal outcomes. After lightweight distillation, reinforcement learning assigns stage-specific credit to reflection triggering, diagnosis, and corrective action. Local validity signals gate trajectory advantages so that intermediate recovery decisions do not indiscriminately inherit terminal outcomes. Across four repository-level software-engineering benchmarks, RIPPLE improves the base policy by an arithmetic mean of 4.8 score points, with no auxiliary critic at deployment. Controlled ablations isolate the benefits of local, stage-aligned credit, and matched-prefix interventions show that critique semantics affect subsequent correction. Recovery gains concentrate where the prefix contains sufficient diagnostic evidence and the repository state remains reversible within the remaining budget.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: Activation-Space Exploration for Visual and Textual Reasoning with RLVR
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Yunan Zeng, Jinhao Jing, Xi Cheng, Yuwang Wang
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: The paper presents Activation-Space Exploration (ASE), enhancing reinforcement learning for visual and textual reasoning by diversifying training rollouts, significantly improving accuracy over existing methods.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) improves visual and textual reasoning by sampling responses, scoring them with an automatic verifier, and updating the policy from the resulting rewards. The policy therefore receives direct learning signals only from trajectories that appear in its rollouts. Yet repeated sampling from the same policy can concentrate on similar reasoning paths, leaving useful alternatives unexplored under a fixed rollout budget. We introduce Activation-Space Exploration (ASE), an online method for diversifying training rollouts. By clustering activation differences between correct and incorrect responses to the same problem, ASE builds a structured bank of latent exploration vectors. Different vectors are then applied to subsequent rollouts to explore alternative reasoning paths. Under the same rollout budget, ASE improves average accuracy over GRPO on Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct by 5.41 and 3.15 percentage points across six visual mathematical and six general visual reasoning benchmarks, respectively. On Qwen3-1.7B-Base, it improves average Mean@8 over GRPO across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks by 4.87 percentage points, with gains also observed on Qwen3-8B-Base.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: AdaRSI: On-Demand Recursive Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Peidong Wang, Ying Chang, Zhiming Ma, Lirong Che, Zihao Liu
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: AdaRSI enhances embodied agents' performance through on-demand recursive self-improvement, achieving significant success rate increases in complex tasks by refining tools and adapting unreliable steps.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Failures in long-horizon embodied tasks can arise from how a vision-language-action model (VLA) is called or from its execution capabilities. We introduce AdaRSI, an on-demand recursive self-improvement framework in which a coding agent first refines its tools and procedures, then adapts sub-steps that remain unreliable after testing alternative instructions and approaches. The agent collects demonstrations, tests their utility through temporary fine-tuning probes, and pools accepted data across tasks to train a specialist VLA that works alongside the original executor. At the end of each development round, its records are summarized into shared experience that guides subsequent diagnosis and data collection. On unseen composite tasks in RoboCasa365, AdaRSI raises success from 4.6% to 13.3%. On perturbed LIBERO-Pro 2.0 tasks, success rises from 32.9% to 49.1%. On RoboCasa365's Composite-Unseen suite, it achieves higher success than adapting every manipulation sub-step, using 34% of the GPU time and 36% of the demonstrations. On a real robot, the agent autonomously collects demonstrations and adapts the executor to recover fallen bottles, improving task completion.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: Process Advantage Signal Shaping: Advantage Construction for Process-Supervised Reinforcement Learning in LLM Reasoners
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Chao Wang, Hongtao Tian, Tao Yang, Yunsheng Shi, Ting Yao
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: The paper presents PASS, a method for constructing policy advantages in reinforcement learning that enhances performance in mathematical reasoning and multi-hop question answering by optimizing feedback normalization and credit resolution.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Dense process supervision provides local evaluations, but leaves open how these scores should become policy advantages. We introduce PASS (Process Advantage Signal Shaping), an advantage-construction method for group-relative policy optimization (GRPO). PASS separately normalizes and fuses reward channels, constructs batch-shared credit units from variation in the fused score trace, and normalizes return-to-go by the remaining unit count. These operations connect feedback scale, credit resolution, and accumulation horizon in a single computation. We evaluate learned process reward model (PRM) feedback for mathematical reasoning and teacher-derived token feedback for multi-hop question answering (QA). Across seven mathematics benchmarks, PASS improves average pass@1 by 4.62 percentage points over outcome-only GRPO with approximately $2\%$ shorter responses. Matched comparisons with Step-GRPO and component ablations further support the choice of shared credit units and residual normalization. On multi-hop QA, PASS improves over process-signal controls across two normalizers; token-level ablations reveal an accuracy--length trade-off: token-level accumulation slightly favors pass@1, while PASS achieves higher pass@8/16 with shorter responses. The results establish the conversion from local process scores to policy advantages as a consequential design choice across distinct supervision sources.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: Inertial Video World Models
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Yuan Gao, Fan Xu, Yu Guo, Yuxu Lu, Zhengru Fang
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: InertialWorld introduces a novel video world model that incorporates inertia as a structural prior for improved autoregressive prediction, enhancing continuity and reducing error accumulation.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: The physical world has inertia: it evolves from what already exists rather than being recreated at every instant. However, many existing video world models lack an explicit mechanism for inertial state evolution, leaving the continuity of motion and structure implicit in video prediction. During autoregressive rollouts, repeated reconstruction can accumulate errors and destabilize the predicted dynamics. To address this limitation, we introduce InertialWorld, an Inertial Video World Model that makes inertia a structural prior for autoregressive prediction: existing scene evidence is carried across time rather than reconstructed at every step. Central to this formulation is Inertial Memory, which turns memory from passive predictive context into an evolving video state with two complementary views: a dense Eulerian grid preserves scene-aligned evidence, while persistent Lagrangian carriers bind local content to learned canonical coordinates. At each step, the model transports the carrier content according to action-conditioned motion, predicts the complete next video state from the transported carriers and dense grid, and uses a learned gate to combine transported and newly predicted content into the memory for the next step. Extensive experiments across multiple domains, including robot manipulation, 3D game simulation, and open-world navigation, demonstrate that InertialWorld achieves competitive autoregressive prediction performance against strong video world model baselines. Codes link: https://github.com/YuanGao-YG/InertialWorld

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: HandRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Hand Pose Estimation
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Zhekai Wang, Luqing Luo, Wenhao Yao, Junjie Lu, Huanan Zhu
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: HandRSI introduces a recursive self-improvement framework for hand pose estimation, significantly enhancing accuracy and reducing jitter through iterative refinement and selective distillation.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Egocentric 3D hand pose estimators still miss hands at the image border, misplace occluded hands and jitter. Such failures are usually fixed by hand-written inference refinements and by fine-tuning, two interdependent steps that are tuned separately. We present HandRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework for a hand pose system that consists of a video estimator and its executable inference harness. In each round, coding agents refine the harness, and a change is accepted only if it improves a composite of all ten benchmark metrics on held-out data without significantly regressing any of them. The accepted harness then guides the estimator through selective distillation, which supervises hand presence and temporal consistency on frames without ground truth, while ground truth supervises pose. Since the updated estimator may change which refinements remain useful, the harness is re-validated on it. Starting from the released ACE-Ego-Hand model, five rounds reduce MPJPE-p by 35% on HOT3D and 11% on ARCTIC and roughly halve jitter. On HOT3D, HandRSI's MPJPE-p is 16% lower than that of ACE-Ego-Hand fine-tuned on the same ground truth. Under a unified protocol, it outperforms nine re-run published methods on all ten metrics of both benchmarks. Hypervolume selection on the accuracy-speed front yields Lite, Medium and Heavy systems running at 20.7 to 41.1 FPS. This report gives the full method, every stage of every round and the complete protocol. Code, evaluator, harnesses and weights are public.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: A Probabilistic Lateral Motion Prediction Model with Improved Response Fidelity for Vehicle-in-the-Loop Simulation
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Xiangyang Ye, Chaosheng Huang, Jinwen Yang, Zhengxian Chen, Jun Li
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: This paper introduces a probabilistic lateral motion prediction model that enhances vehicle response fidelity in VIL simulations, achieving significant reductions in lateral-position and velocity prediction errors.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) simulation requires a lateral dynamics model that accurately reproduces vehicle responses and reliably generates horizontal lateral-position and heading commands through recursive integration. This paper presents a probabilistic lateral motion prediction model with improved response fidelity. A two-degree-of-freedom vehicle model provides the physical prior, while a recurrent neural network learns correlated residual corrections to lateral acceleration and yaw rate. To maintain prediction fidelity during recursive motion generation, multistep rollout training feeds corrected responses into subsequent states and histories and directly penalizes accumulated lateral-velocity error. A conditional Gaussian characterizes response uncertainty, which is propagated to lateral-response, position, and heading predictions through augmented-state linearization. Evaluation results demonstrate improved lateral-response and integrated-motion prediction. Compared with the Deep Dynamics lateral adaptation, the proposed model reduces mean lateral-position root-mean-square error (RMSE) from 0.596 m to 0.483 m, an improvement of 19.0%, while reducing mean lateral-velocity RMSE from 0.0469 m/s to 0.0441 m/s. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining physical priors, probabilistic residual learning, and multistep rollout training for response-faithful lateral motion prediction.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: What Can a VLA Learn from the Agent That Calls It? Task-Level Experience Distillation for Embodied Navigation
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Jinze Tao, Yuxiao Han, Kangkang Dong, Yancong Wei, Xiaojun Zhu
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: The H2E method enhances VLA navigation by distilling task-level experiences from an LLM planner, improving success rates and efficiency without LLM dependency during testing.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models drive the robot directly from camera views, yet a VLA alone shows three typical failures. It walks past the goal, stops before reaching it, and rarely recovers after going off track. Pairing a VLA with a large language model (LLM) planner fixes these failures, but queries the LLM throughout every episode, adding token costs and latency. We introduce Harness-to-Executor (H2E), a task-level distillation method that pairs an LLM planner and a frozen VLA as a heterogeneous training agent, keeps only sessions that reach the goal, and then trains a VLA alone on them so no LLM is used at test time. In these sessions, the planner gives sub-instructions and moves the robot with its own tools, detours are common, and the planner decides when to stop. H2E therefore labels every motion as a VLA action for the original task, whoever made it. It masks the loss on steps moving away from the goal and assigns end labels to states near it, so the VLA learns where the task ends. H2E sets a new state of the art on REVERIE-CE and NavRAG-CE. It raises an 8B VLA's success rate by 15.6% and 11.1% respectively, surpassing a method trained on 10M samples. The distilled VLA exceeds its agent on unseen episodes with zero LLM tokens and runs 3.7 times faster.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: Fast Inference-Time Policy Refinement via Action-Affine World Models
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Run Wang, Yilin Mo, Liang Wu
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: The paper presents an action-affine world model for fast refinement of frozen imitation policies, achieving high success rates in manipulation tasks with minimal latency.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Imitation policies can fail through compounding errors, while existing refinement methods often require additional on-policy learning or expensive online planning. Our key insight is to model the response to small corrections around a policy proposal in an affine form that enables fast optimization. We refine a frozen imitation policy using an \textit{action-affine world model} (A\textsuperscript{2}WM), trained offline from perturbed policy rollouts. Conditioned on history and the proposal, the model directly predicts a nominal trajectory and a linear action response over the full horizon. With quadratic costs and linear constraints, refinement becomes a cheap quadratic program (QP), requiring only one model evaluation and one QP solve per control step. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to combine an action-affine world model with QP-based inference-time refinement of frozen imitation policies. Across four manipulation tasks, our framework achieves the highest success rate among evaluated baselines, adding only 4.2 ms of mean refinement latency per control step, excluding base-policy sampling.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: Agentic In-Context Learning: What Algorithms Can Transformers Learn in Closed-Loop Interaction?
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Shiguang Wu, Yaqing Wang, Quanming Yao
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: The paper introduces Agentic In-Context Learning (Agentic ICL), where Transformers learn interactively through decision-making, optimizing rewards to influence behavior and decision policies.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: The learning algorithm view of in-context learning (ICL) studies how fixed-parameter Transformers learn from supplied examples. Language model agents extend this setting through interaction: their actions determine what evidence enters context next. We call this regime Agentic In-Context Learning (Agentic ICL). Existing studies largely depend on externally supplied contexts or reward-bearing interaction histories, while work on general tool-using agents lacks a learning algorithm view. We represent an interactive learner by its state, update, and decision rule, covering active learning, bandits, and online reinforcement learning (RL). For expressivity, we construct causal Transformers that approximate these algorithms over a finite horizon, and bound the resulting loss in return. For training, we characterize when optimizing process rewards preserves behavior that maximizes the final outcome. Distillation experiments show that Transformers can learn to execute three representative recursions. We then train models from outcome or process rewards without oracle action or state targets, as in RL post-training. Different rewards yield distinct decision policies. Improving the alignment of process supervision with outcome-optimal action preferences shifts learned decisions accordingly. Such behavioral differences persist in a pretrained language model across textual paraphrases.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).title: Agent-Centric Observation Adaptation for Robust Visual Control under Dynamic Perturbations
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).authors_text: Zhengru Fang, Yu Guo, Huanhuan Lou, Fei Liu, Yuang Zhang
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: The paper presents ACO-MoE, a method that enhances visual control under dynamic perturbations, significantly improving task success rates and returns in robotic applications.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Visual control maps visual streams to actions in reinforcement learning and vision-language-action (VLA) policies. Changing weather, noise, blur, and compression can obscure different task cues within one episode. Existing control benchmarks mainly test scene distractions, while generic restorers optimize whole-image fidelity. We introduce the Visual Degraded Control Suite (VDCS) to evaluate seven degradations under Markov switching. We propose Agent-Centric Observations with Mixture-of-Experts (ACO-MoE), which routes each frame to a repair expert, restores RGB content, and composes task-relevant foregrounds. On eight VDCS tasks, corruption lowers DreamerV3's mean return from 769 to 562. ACO-MoE raises it to 730, recovering 81.2% of the lost return. It also improves returns on DMC-GB and RoboSuite and retains 70% to 97% of clean-input mean return under six unseen perturbation families. We train ACO-MoE on robot demonstrations and deploy it with a 3B-parameter VLA policy on a Piper arm for cube placement in blue and white boxes and cup placement on a coaster. On the blue-box and cup tasks, motion blur and physical low light with added noise reduce success from 100% to at most 10%. ACO-MoE raises success to 75% to 95% over 20 trials per task and condition.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Lyapunov-Inspired Sustained Balance on Dynamically Responsive Supports
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Changyan Li, Guiyin Tian, Jing Xia, Shiyan Hu
潘佳老师实验室.summary: The paper presents LISST, a learning framework for maintaining balance on responsive supports by coordinating body stabilization and support motion suppression through a Lyapunov-inspired approach.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Conventional balance formulations often assume a rigid, stationary support, decoupling body stabilization from support motion. This assumption becomes inadequate on mechanically responsive supports, creating a coupled control challenge: corrective body motions intended to restore equilibrium can also excite support motion. We formulate sustained balance as a coupled regulation problem that coordinates equilibrium restoration with suppression of motion induced by the robot's own corrections. We introduce LISST (Lyapunov-Inspired Sustained Stabilization), a learning framework that accounts for how earlier actions shape the conditions for subsequent corrections. It uses recent observations to support immediate adjustments and longer histories to characterize persistent motion, with physical supervision relating the learned representation to robot-support behavior. To evaluate corrective actions, LISST uses coupled dynamics to assess both imbalance and the direction of motion. A Lyapunov-inspired criterion measures progress over finite windows, accommodating the transients required to restore balance. This physical evaluation guides joint-level policy learning through backpropagation through differentiable model rollouts. Privileged guidance focuses training on difficult states reached by the deployment policy and is transferred through distillation. The resulting policy operates using only onboard proprioception. Real-world experiments demonstrate that LISST maintains balance while limiting residual oscillations during continuous interaction with a dynamically responsive support. Video: youtu.be/iGHU7S4wPyw.

潘佳老师实验室.title: DualTopo: Spatio-Temporal Lane Graph Generation with Dual Latent World Models and Parallel Query Supervision
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Yiming Yang, Hongbin Lin, Yueru Luo, Suzhong Fu, Chao Zheng
潘佳老师实验室.summary: DualTopo introduces a dual latent world model framework for enhanced spatiotemporal lane graph generation, addressing query supervision and boundary information loss in autonomous driving.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Lane topology reasoning constructs a spatiotemporal road graph G = (V, E) in bird's-eye view (BEV), providing structured road representations for planning-oriented autonomous driving. Stream-based methods propagate temporal cues at both the query and BEV levels, yet suffer from two critical limitations: (1) initialized queries receive insufficient supervision, as temporal queries dominate Hungarian matching and leave them undertrained; and (2) temporal propagation is weakened by BEV boundary information loss during feature warping. Since initialized queries serve as propagation anchors, particularly at the first frame, these deficiencies compound across frames and degrade graph generation quality. We propose DualTopo, a spatio-temporal lane graph generation framework with dual latent world models and dual parallel decoder pathways. The dual-pathway decoder supervises temporal and initialized queries concurrently, ensuring initialized queries are well-trained and serve as reliable anchors. Dual latent world models conditioned on ego-motion propagate latent state representations from past observations to the present, substantially improving spatiotemporal graph generation. Extensive experiments on OpenLane-V2 demonstrate leading lane detection accuracy and competitive topology graph prediction. Code is available at https://github.com/YimingYang23/DualTopo.

潘佳老师实验室.title: PCGRL for Complex Platformers: Synthesizing Playable and Diverse Levels via Inflated Envelopes and Forward Curricula
潘佳老师实验室.summary: The paper introduces a physics-aware, curriculum-guided PCGRL framework that enhances level diversity and solvability in complex platformers by addressing exploration bottlenecks and reward sparsity.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Procedural Content Generation via Reinforcement Learning (PCGRL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for automated game development. However, existing PCGRL frameworks still suffer from severe exploration bottlenecks and scaling limitations when faced with long-sequence generation tasks governed by strict rigid-body rules and non-linear kinematic boundaries (e.g., platformer constraints). Consequently, traditional approaches frequently fail to maintain reliable level solvability on large-scale canvases. To address these challenges, we present a physics-aware, curriculum-guided PCGRL framework. First, we construct an "Inflated Volume Envelope" mechanism, which provides a physics-constrained representation that incorporates continuous kinematic feasibility into the discrete state space of the MDP. Second, to alleviate the sparse reward challenge induced by extremely long decision sequences, we introduce intermediate state-transition feedback and a multi-stage forward extension curriculum learning framework, enabling informative value estimation and stable credit assignment over long-horizon trajectories. Finally, to resolve the issue where deterministic policies after convergence generate highly monotonous map paths with a lack of diversity, we activate high-entropy stochastic inference during the synthesis phase, regularized by a post-hoc parallel rejection filtering mechanism. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework significantly enhances structural diversity while maintaining high physical playability across multi-scale environments. Comparative evaluations across multi-scale canvases demonstrate that our framework maintains superior convergence stability and dimensional scalability, reliably synthesizing solvable levels where traditional PCGRL baselines degrade.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Controllable Texture Tiling with Transformed RoPE-Enhanced Diffusion Models
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Junrong Huang, Zhiyuan Zhang, Rui Tang, Hongbo Fu, Jing Liao
潘佳老师实验室.summary: This paper presents a novel framework using Diffusion Transformers for high-fidelity texture tiling, enhancing control and fidelity through innovative embedding and attention mechanisms.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Realistic integration of user-specified textures into scene images is a fundamental task in computer graphics and image editing. While existing material transfer and reference-guided inpainting methods can edit surface appearances, they often fail to address the specific requirements of texture tiling. This task necessitates precisely repeating a reference pattern according to user-defined parameters such as frequency, orientation, and scale. Furthermore, current generative approaches often struggle to maintain the structural fidelity of the reference texture, limited by either destructive pixel-level resampling or the lack of fine-grained spatial information in semantic image encoders, and they frequently fail to preserve the coherent lighting and geometry of the original scene. In this paper, we propose a novel framework for controllable and high-fidelity texture tiling based on Diffusion Transformers. Our approach introduces two key technical innovations to decouple spatial manipulation from content generation. First, we propose a Coordinate-Transformed Rotary Embedding mechanism. By applying 2D affine transformations directly to the relative positional embeddings between the target latent and the image condition, we achieve precise control over tiling patterns without explicit pixel warping, thereby utilizing the full information of the reference condition without degradation. Second, a Disjoint Attention Mask is employed to shield reference features from semantic leakage. This preserves structural integrity while seamlessly blending the synthesized texture with the scene's original lighting and geometry. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both control accuracy and texture fidelity.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Zero-Shot Compositional Generalization for Embodied Manipulation
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Baicheng Li, Wenkang Qin, Youqi Pan, Dongxiao Mao, Yukun Zhou
潘佳老师实验室.summary: The paper presents a geometry-supervised framework enabling zero-shot compositional generalization in robotic manipulation by leveraging demonstrated commands across different robot embodiments without requiring joint labels.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Robot demonstrations are collected on different embodiments, leaving many robot-skill combinations unobserved. Pooling these data shares visual knowledge, while joint labels remain tied to the demonstrating kinematic chain. We propose a geometry-supervised training framework for zero-shot composition of familiar robots and skills. The central insight is that a demonstrated command provides a tool-space target for every robot that can realize it. Calibrated forward kinematics supplies this supervision to foreign native action interfaces without their joint labels for that skill. Native reconstruction retains demonstrated configurations, and positive reachability checks select targets for cross-robot supervision. A visual policy learns to predict shared actions and executes through the target robot's native decoder. During policy learning, one prediction receives geometric supervision through both source and foreign native realizations. Matched supervision controls, repeated policy training and evaluations across three backbones and two simulators demonstrate improved transfer to missing robot-task combinations.

潘佳老师实验室.title: SpatialCast: Reading the 3D World via Cast Shadows
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Enhan Li, Jinghao Zhou, Jiaze Zhang, Hongyang Du
潘佳老师实验室.summary: SpatialCast is a benchmark utilizing cast shadows to evaluate multimodal large language models' spatial reasoning abilities through tasks assessing scene consistency and physical changes.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: As multimodal large language models (MLLMs) advance toward understanding and interacting with the physical world, spatial reasoning becomes essential for understanding scene structure and anticipating the effects of physical changes. Existing spatial benchmarks have made substantial progress in evaluating spatial relations, memory, and viewpoint reasoning, but less systematically assess how models connect physical scene conditions with visual observations. We introduce SpatialCast, a benchmark that uses cast shadows to evaluate this ability. Cast shadows provide observable evidence of a 3D scene. Their image appearance depends on object geometry and pose, illumination, and viewpoint. We examine this relationship through three complementary tasks that assess scene-projection consistency, predict intervention-induced changes, and infer the physical changes behind visual transitions. The benchmark contains 21,000 synthetic questions with separate scene and geometry test partitions, complemented by 200 SpatialCast-Real questions from 20 photographed scenes. Evaluations show that closed-source MLLMs outperform general-purpose open-weight MLLMs and MLLMs designed for spatial reasoning, which remain near chance on the synthetic benchmark, while even strong closed-source models struggle with shadow-length and light-height judgments. We also use SpatialCast training data for GRPO post-training, improving open-weight MLLM performance on the benchmark. Further evaluations show improvements on several external spatial benchmarks, suggesting transfer of the learned capabilities. These experiments support SpatialCast as a controlled resource for diagnosing spatial reasoning capabilities and studying their learning and generalization.

潘佳老师实验室.title: EvoSkill-S1: Evolving Reusable Skills with Genetic-Inspired Operators
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Yujun Wang, Jiqiang Li, Yinuo Lu, Jinhe Bi, Aniri
潘佳老师实验室.summary: EvoSkill-S1 introduces a genetic-inspired framework for evolving reusable skills in language-model agents, enhancing problem-solving effectiveness through direct skill evolution and selective retention.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Reusable skills allow language-model agents to accumulate and reuse problem-solving experience. However, most existing methods improve a skill bank only indirectly through rollout-driven accumulation and heuristic reflection, often resulting in shallow and weakly controlled updates. We present EvoSkill-S1, an RL-driven framework that instead treats reusable skills themselves as the direct objects of evolution. Given hard-negative failures, EvoSkill-S1 selects parent skills and transforms them into candidate child skills through five genetic-inspired operators: revision, cross-revision, mutation, dual-reflection, and crossover. Downstream task rewards train the skill evolver to generate more effective child skills, while evaluator-guided write-back selectively retains beneficial updates. Complementary Skill Bank Fusion consolidates operator-specific banks to exploit their distinct recovery patterns, while a Procedural Skill Interface supports transfer to unseen problems. Across all reported math and code benchmarks, EvoSkill-S1 improves the corresponding initialized skill banks under both Qwen and GPT-family solvers, with relative gains of up to 12.39%. Compared with the strongest external baseline without direct skill evolution, the largest relative improvement reaches 20.39%.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Diagnosing and Correcting Bias in MLLM for Long Video Understanding
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Xusheng Liang, Jianqiao Sun, Hao Zhang, Yulei Niu, Hengshuang Zhao
潘佳老师实验室.summary: The paper introduces S-MME for diagnosing bias in MLLMs and proposes CLEAR, a framework to enhance long-video question answering by mitigating misleading cues.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Long-video question answering is challenging since the answer often hinges on a few decisive moments scattered throughout the video, while memory constraints force Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to sample frames at extremely low rates, resulting in sparsity that risks omitting key evidence. Though aggressively enlarging the context size is intuitive, we argue that performance remains fundamentally constrained by the bias, i.e., the misleading cues caused by spurious linguistic correlations and salient yet irrelevant visual observations. In this paper, we first introduce S-MME, a benchmark designed to systematically diagnose shortcut-biased behavior in MLLMs. To mitigate this failure, we further propose a training-free framework, Counterfactual Long-video Evidence-Aware Reasoning (CLEAR). By treating the full video-question pair as a complete view, CLEAR estimates bias effects via augmented views by only keeping the question or locally salient visual clips. Then, we intervene hidden states to mitigate the discrepancy at inference such that the correct answer can be predicted confidently. With experimental studies across five benchmarks, we show that our method is generalizable and can be integrated in different MLLMs, yielding consistent gains in prediction and robustness. We hope CLEAR can offer a complementary direction in test-time scaling for long-video understanding.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Activation-Space Exploration for Visual and Textual Reasoning with RLVR
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Yunan Zeng, Jinhao Jing, Xi Cheng, Yuwang Wang
潘佳老师实验室.summary: The paper presents Activation-Space Exploration (ASE), enhancing reinforcement learning for visual and textual reasoning by diversifying training rollouts, significantly improving accuracy over existing methods.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) improves visual and textual reasoning by sampling responses, scoring them with an automatic verifier, and updating the policy from the resulting rewards. The policy therefore receives direct learning signals only from trajectories that appear in its rollouts. Yet repeated sampling from the same policy can concentrate on similar reasoning paths, leaving useful alternatives unexplored under a fixed rollout budget. We introduce Activation-Space Exploration (ASE), an online method for diversifying training rollouts. By clustering activation differences between correct and incorrect responses to the same problem, ASE builds a structured bank of latent exploration vectors. Different vectors are then applied to subsequent rollouts to explore alternative reasoning paths. Under the same rollout budget, ASE improves average accuracy over GRPO on Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct by 5.41 and 3.15 percentage points across six visual mathematical and six general visual reasoning benchmarks, respectively. On Qwen3-1.7B-Base, it improves average Mean@8 over GRPO across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks by 4.87 percentage points, with gains also observed on Qwen3-8B-Base.

潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Yuan Gao, Fan Xu, Yu Guo, Yuxu Lu, Zhengru Fang
潘佳老师实验室.summary: InertialWorld introduces a novel video world model that incorporates inertia as a structural prior for improved autoregressive prediction, enhancing continuity and reducing error accumulation.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: The physical world has inertia: it evolves from what already exists rather than being recreated at every instant. However, many existing video world models lack an explicit mechanism for inertial state evolution, leaving the continuity of motion and structure implicit in video prediction. During autoregressive rollouts, repeated reconstruction can accumulate errors and destabilize the predicted dynamics. To address this limitation, we introduce InertialWorld, an Inertial Video World Model that makes inertia a structural prior for autoregressive prediction: existing scene evidence is carried across time rather than reconstructed at every step. Central to this formulation is Inertial Memory, which turns memory from passive predictive context into an evolving video state with two complementary views: a dense Eulerian grid preserves scene-aligned evidence, while persistent Lagrangian carriers bind local content to learned canonical coordinates. At each step, the model transports the carrier content according to action-conditioned motion, predicts the complete next video state from the transported carriers and dense grid, and uses a learned gate to combine transported and newly predicted content into the memory for the next step. Codes link: https://github.com/YuanGao-YG/InertialWorld

潘佳老师实验室.title: EvoDisco: Strategy Discovery for Evolving Agent Memory
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Mingyang Liu, Qingcan Kang, Shixiong Kai, Kaichao Liang, Xiaojin Fu
潘佳老师实验室.summary: EvoDisco enhances agent memory evolution by enabling dynamic selection and instantiation of memory transformation operators, significantly outperforming existing memory methods in various tasks.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Large language model agents accumulate experience in memory, and how that memory evolves during interaction is as important as what it stores. Recent methods update memory online, yet both the operators that transform memory and the rules that select them remain fixed by design. We propose EvoDisco, which formulates agent memory evolution as evolutionary strategy discovery: the agent must discover which operator to apply, when to apply it, and how to instantiate it, rather than rewriting memory under a static operator schedule. A learnable policy conditions on the current memory state and recent task history, then selects and instantiates one of four semantic operators---Abstract, Refine, Bridge, and Reframe---which respectively compress related memories, decompose overloaded entries, connect weakly linked experiences, and reorganize retrieved reasoning chains. The policy is updated with a bi-level fitness. An inner signal scores each transformation using a retrieval-quality improvement regularized by memory complexity. An outer signal scores strategic efficacy over a window of past decisions, combining historical operator-utility regret, utility-prediction error, and selection diversity. Under a one-pass online plus frozen-transfer protocol on ALFWorld, WebShop, and LifelongAgentBench (OS and DB), EvoDisco improves over strong memory baselines including MemP and MemRL. The largest gains are on ALFWorld ($+8.8$ online / $+12.9$ frozen-transfer points over MemP; $+16.4$ / $+17.9$ over MemRL). Ablations attribute these gains to both fitness levels and the operator library.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Let the Mind Conceive, Let the Hand Achieve: Coupling Grounded Action and Progress Evaluation for Long-Horizon Manipulation
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Youpeng Wen, Gang Wang, Tianyu Huang, Weiwei Zhang, Zhijian Huang
潘佳老师实验室.summary: Orchestra enhances robot manipulation by effectively managing task planning, execution, and progress evaluation, achieving significant improvements in multi-step instruction execution success rates.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: A robot following a multi-step instruction needs to act on the right objects in the right order, even as the scene changes. It must also maintain awareness of task progress and determine when to advance. To address these challenges, we introduce Orchestra, an agent harness that separates task planning and execution management from action generation. Orchestra decomposes a complete multimodal instruction into ordered subtasks, tracks completed steps, and updates the locations of relevant objects and destinations during execution. It maintains a shared context containing the active subtask, spatial grounding, and recent observations. An action policy uses this context to generate actions, while a separately trained progress evaluator estimates when to advance to the next subtask. To evaluate whether robots trained on atomic instructions and short trajectories can execute longer subtask sequences, we introduce a benchmark named RMBench-Compose. Orchestra achieves a mean success rate of $68.22\%$ across nine RMBench tasks, outperforming Mem-0 by $26.22$ percentage points. On RMBench-Compose, it achieves an Average Success Length (ASL) of $7.35$ subtasks, $2.46$ times that of HarnessVLA. Across four real-world multi-step tasks, it improves mean ASL by $25.0\%$ over Orchestra using the base $π_{0.5}$ policy. These results show that Orchestra helps robots carry out longer sequences of subtasks while preserving the requested subtask order and acting on the specified objects. Our code and project page are available at https://youpengwen.github.io/Orchestra

潘佳老师实验室.title: Agent-Centric Observation Adaptation for Robust Visual Control under Dynamic Perturbations
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Zhengru Fang, Yu Guo, Huanhuan Lou, Fei Liu, Yuang Zhang
潘佳老师实验室.summary: The paper presents ACO-MoE, a method that enhances visual control under dynamic perturbations, significantly improving task success rates and returns in robotic applications.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Visual control maps visual streams to actions in reinforcement learning and vision-language-action (VLA) policies. Changing weather, noise, blur, and compression can obscure different task cues within one episode. Existing control benchmarks mainly test scene distractions, while generic restorers optimize whole-image fidelity. We introduce the Visual Degraded Control Suite (VDCS) to evaluate seven degradations under Markov switching. We propose Agent-Centric Observations with Mixture-of-Experts (ACO-MoE), which routes each frame to a repair expert, restores RGB content, and composes task-relevant foregrounds. On eight VDCS tasks, corruption lowers DreamerV3's mean return from 769 to 562. ACO-MoE raises it to 730, recovering 81.2% of the lost return. It also improves returns on DMC-GB and RoboSuite and retains 70% to 97% of clean-input mean return under six unseen perturbation families. We train ACO-MoE on robot demonstrations and deploy it with a 3B-parameter VLA policy on a Piper arm for cube placement in blue and white boxes and cup placement on a coaster. On the blue-box and cup tasks, motion blur and physical low light with added noise reduce success from 100% to at most 10%. ACO-MoE raises success to 75% to 95% over 20 trials per task and condition.

机器人研究所.title: Distilling World Action Models for Efficient Bimanual Manipulation via Anchored Path Matching
机器人研究所.authors_text: Jialong Liu, Junjie He, Yandu Chen, Bin Zhou, Heng Su
机器人研究所.summary: The paper presents Anchored Path Matching (APM), enhancing World Action Models for bimanual manipulation by improving trajectory accuracy and efficiency in robot actions through targeted gradient updates.
机器人研究所.debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) jointly generate future video and robot actions through iterative denoising. Few-step distillation reduces the number of model evaluations, but its coarse updates can move the student away from the teacher's trajectory. We propose Anchored Path Matching (APM), which supervises endpoint and short-transition predictions from states reached by the student. From each state, we continue the teacher to zero noise and use its endpoint and first intermediate state as targets. Modality-routed adapters learn to match both targets from the same starting state. When the two gradients conflict, anchor-priority updates preserve the endpoint gradient and remove the opposing component of the local gradient within each modality. One checkpoint supports 1-, 2-, and 4-step joint generation. The sampling budget can be chosen at deployment without retraining or teacher queries. On RoboTwin 2.0, we train only on Clean demonstrations and evaluate directly on the domain-randomized Random setting. At one step, APM improves closed-loop success over continued base distillation at matched inference budgets by 2.0 percentage points on Clean and 1.4 on Random. Video peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) rises from 30.169 to 32.317 dB, with gains in structural similarity (SSIM) and learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS). On two real-robot tasks, APM improves success over the one-step teacher and reduces control-cycle latency by $21.3\times$ relative to the eight-step teacher.Project page: https://jialonglong.github.io/Anchored-Path-Matching/.

机器人研究所.title: CoSphere-SLAM: Multi-Agent Panoramic Gaussian Splatting SLAM with Spherical Loop Closure
机器人研究所.authors_text: Qi Shao, Zhihao Cao, Shuhao Zhai, Taoyu Wu, Zhuoxiao Li
机器人研究所.summary: CoSphere-SLAM introduces a multi-agent Gaussian splatting framework for panoramic SLAM that effectively addresses loop closure and scale drift challenges, achieving superior mapping accuracy.
机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Dense collaborative mapping is essential for search and rescue, building inspection, and warehouse automation, where panoramic cameras capture the entire surroundings in a single frame. Unlike pinhole agents that share views only at similar headings, panoramic agents observe overlapping scenes at any 3D orientation, yet searching full rotations also produces mutually consistent false loop closures across distinct symmetric rooms. Moreover, continuous monocular scale drift splits rigidly merged maps at revisited surfaces, while depth noise at short baselines distorts loop translation directions. To address these challenges, we propose CoSphere-SLAM, the first multi-agent Gaussian splatting SLAM framework for panoramic cameras, whose spherical loop closure aligns spherical features over $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ via fast Fourier correlation across arbitrary orientations and rejects symmetric false closures through global $\mathrm{Sim}(3)$ consensus. Building on these closures, directional global optimization solves a per-keyframe $\mathrm{Sim}(3)$ pose graph with log-scale regularization to correct scale drift while separating optical-flow translation directions from depth-based magnitudes. Finally, omnidirectional Gaussian fusion transforms each Gaussian with its keyframe similarity and renders Gaussians at their maximum ray response to jointly refine poses and maps. Experiments on indoor and cross-session multi-agent panoramic benchmarks demonstrate that CoSphere-SLAM achieves state-of-the-art trajectory accuracy and rendering quality among single-agent and multi-agent methods. Project website: https://cosphere-slam.github.io.

机器人研究所.title: RoboTeam: Benchmarking Vision-Based Multi-Agent Control of Many Robot Arms in Real Time
机器人研究所.authors_text: Changxuan Fan, Zhongwei Xie, Boyi Zhang, Shaoli Hu, Chang Xu
机器人研究所.summary: RoboTeam introduces a real-time benchmark for vision-based control of 4 to 16 robot arms, evaluating various agent systems on complex, long-duration tasks without pausing the environment.
机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Multimodal agents can now control robot arms by calling tools and writing code. Existing benchmarks fall short in three ways: most test one or two arms on short tasks, many pause the world while the agent thinks, and many give it ground-truth object positions. We present RoboTeam, a simulated benchmark where agents control 4 to 16 robot arms in real time from camera images alone. Its 36 tasks are long jobs that the arms must do together, such as passing timbers or building a picture from hundreds of cubes. We start from the most flexible agent system, the adaptive system, where one agent decides when to fork delegates. With it, gpt-6.1-sol and opus-5.5 complete 28 and 27 tasks, and four other models at most 3. But at a high price: a typical task takes gpt-6.1-sol 3.5 hours and 218 million input tokens, and a third of its steps fail at least once and must be retried. We then compare it with three fixed systems: single-agent, hierarchical, and decentralized. All four complete a similar number of tasks but differ in time and tokens. The hierarchical and decentralized systems are faster but use up to 1.9 times the tokens, and the single agent uses fewer tokens but takes 1.6 times as long, so the adaptive system lies between them. Even so, no model or system is yet fast, cheap, and reliable at once. RoboTeam measures these limits where earlier benchmarks cannot: long multi-arm jobs, camera images only, and a world that never pauses.

机器人研究所.title: Controllable Texture Tiling with Transformed RoPE-Enhanced Diffusion Models
机器人研究所.authors_text: Junrong Huang, Zhiyuan Zhang, Rui Tang, Hongbo Fu, Jing Liao
机器人研究所.summary: This paper presents a novel framework using Diffusion Transformers for high-fidelity texture tiling, enhancing control and fidelity through innovative embedding and attention mechanisms.
机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Realistic integration of user-specified textures into scene images is a fundamental task in computer graphics and image editing. While existing material transfer and reference-guided inpainting methods can edit surface appearances, they often fail to address the specific requirements of texture tiling. This task necessitates precisely repeating a reference pattern according to user-defined parameters such as frequency, orientation, and scale. Furthermore, current generative approaches often struggle to maintain the structural fidelity of the reference texture, limited by either destructive pixel-level resampling or the lack of fine-grained spatial information in semantic image encoders, and they frequently fail to preserve the coherent lighting and geometry of the original scene. In this paper, we propose a novel framework for controllable and high-fidelity texture tiling based on Diffusion Transformers. Our approach introduces two key technical innovations to decouple spatial manipulation from content generation. First, we propose a Coordinate-Transformed Rotary Embedding mechanism. By applying 2D affine transformations directly to the relative positional embeddings between the target latent and the image condition, we achieve precise control over tiling patterns without explicit pixel warping, thereby utilizing the full information of the reference condition without degradation. Second, a Disjoint Attention Mask is employed to shield reference features from semantic leakage. This preserves structural integrity while seamlessly blending the synthesized texture with the scene's original lighting and geometry. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both control accuracy and texture fidelity.

机器人研究所.title: HolisticMotion: Holistic Modeling for Motion Reconstruction from Sparse Tracking
机器人研究所.authors_text: Runzhen Liu, Chuhua Xian, Hongmin Cai, Fa-Ting Hong
机器人研究所.summary: HolisticMotion enhances full-body motion reconstruction from sparse tracking by employing a unified skeletal model, curriculum masking, body partitioning, and Kinematic Attention, achieving superior accuracy.
机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Reconstructing full-body motion from sparse tracking signals is crucial for immersive AR/VR applications. Existing methods predominantly adopt a sensor-centric observation perspective, learning full-body representations primarily under sparse conditioning, while additional joint observations available during training remain underutilized as inputs. We propose HolisticMotion, which shifts the modeling perspective toward holistic full-body modeling by treating every joint as a potential input source within a unified skeletal layout. Guided by this holistic perspective, we introduce three complementary designs. First, a curriculum masking strategy bridges full-body motion learning and sparse inference by gradually shifting training from a mixture of masked full-body and sparse inputs to exclusively sparse inputs. Second, body partitioning models region dynamics and helps preserve local motion cues. Third, Kinematic Attention coordinates body regions by combining dynamic spatial interactions with learnable structural priors inspired by the kinematic tree. Experiments on AMASS and HPS demonstrate competitive reconstruction performance across various tracking protocols, with the lowest positional errors among the compared methods. The unified representation also accommodates additional wearable sensors, yielding further improvements in reconstruction accuracy and motion smoothness.

机器人研究所.title: Reading Scene States: Uncovering Safety Failures in Vision-Language Models
机器人研究所.authors_text: Tongxi Wu, Yuyang Cheng, Jiacheng Xian, Menglin Yang, Kai Chen
机器人研究所.summary: The paper identifies a safety vulnerability in vision-language models, introducing SceneSafetyBench and S3TA, which exploit scene states to elicit harmful assistance with high success rates.
机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can provide harmful assistance by interpreting visual events, even without an explicit request for the underlying harmful objective. We identify this \textbf{scene-state safety vulnerability} and introduce \textbf{SceneSafetyBench}, comprising 375 image--question pairs spanning Initial, Medium, and Ultimate scene states and five visual presentations. Across eight VLMs, scene-state inputs elicit harmful assistance with attack success rates (ASRs) of 45.6--72.3\%. Comparative analysis across three VLMs shows that scene-state inputs most closely resemble QR-related images in their layer-wise safety-related signal profiles, while exhibiting lower average late-layer readouts and distinct signal dynamics during generation. To turn this vulnerability into a systematic attack, we propose \textbf{S3TA}, which translates harmful objectives into scene states, queries image--question pairs independently, and assembles the responses. On seven MM-SafetyBench categories across eight open-weight and commercial VLMs, S3TA achieves a model-average ASR of \textbf{71.2\%, exceeding the strongest baseline by 6.1 percentage points}. Text-side filters and visual moderation provide limited protection. These findings highlight the need to safeguard the assistance models infer through scene-grounded reasoning, beyond screening input content.

机器人研究所.title: TCP4D: A Unified Tool-Center-Point Tracking and Generation Model for Robot Manipulation
机器人研究所.authors_text: Haosong Peng, Xiangyang Liu, Zhengshen Zhang, Yunfeng Fan, Tianyu Qi
机器人研究所.summary: TCP4D is a unified model that tracks and generates robot manipulation trajectories from monocular videos, achieving high accuracy and adaptability across different robot embodiments.
机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Robot manipulation videos provide a rich visual experience, yet recovering robot action and gripper-state annotations from RGB observations still remains challenging. Using the embodiment-agnostic tool-center-point (TCP) pose as the action space, we present TCP4D, a unified model in which a shared 4D scene representation both tracks observed TCP motion and generates future TCP trajectories. Given a monocular video and initial 2D TCP queries, the tracker directly recovers metric TCP poses in SE(3) and gripper states alongside scene geometry and camera parameters. The generator samples local features from the same 4D representation along the recovered TCP tracks, then combines them with robot observations and language instructions to predict future TCP states. Our new cross-embodiment augmentation pipeline converts existing RGB videos into demonstrations for alternative embodiments by retargeting the recovered motion and synthesizing the corresponding observations, without recorded source-robot states. Experiments show that the tracker achieves absolute trajectory errors of 7.60 and 16.07 mm on DROID and RoboLab and adapts to a new embodiment with only ten demonstrations. The generator achieves 69.19% mean success on RoboTwin and outperforms well-established policy models on two real-world tasks, while joint training on source and augmented demonstrations improves target-robot success by 41.5% over augmented-only training.

机器人研究所.title: Outcome-Balanced PPO and Policy-Induced Flow Rectification for Flow-Based VLA Policies
机器人研究所.authors_text: Yuhan Wang, Ruiyang Wang, Jiaguan Zhu
机器人研究所.summary: The paper presents an RL framework combining Outcome-Balanced PPO and flow rectification to enhance flow-based VLA policies, improving task success rates in simulations.
机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables post-training of flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) policies by optimizing expected task return through environment interaction. However, this optimization raises two challenges: policy updates can alter the velocity-field geometry underlying the score approximation used for stochastic transitions, and sparse multi-task rollouts can yield uneven learning signals across tasks and advantage signs. We introduce an RL framework that combines Outcome-Balanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with policy-induced flow rectification. Outcome-Balanced PPO reweights positive advantages using task success-rate estimates and rescales positive and negative advantages while preserving their signs. Policy-induced rectification periodically fits a linear-bridge flow to ODE endpoint pairs generated by the current policy, refreshing the representation used in subsequent stochastic optimization. We evaluate the framework on simulated manipulation benchmarks and additionally study a component combination in a Real2Sim2Real task, examining task performance, optimization behavior, and flow consistency. The proposed framework improves success rates over the evaluated baselines across the simulated benchmarks.

机器人研究所.title: Traffic Sign Recognition in Autonomous Driving: Dataset, Benchmark, and Field Experiment
机器人研究所.authors_text: Guoyang Zhao, Weiqing Qi, Kai Zhang, Chenguang Zhang, Zeying Gong
机器人研究所.summary: The paper introduces TS-1M, a comprehensive traffic sign dataset and benchmark for evaluating TSR models' robustness to challenges in autonomous driving, revealing key insights into model performance.
机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Traffic Sign Recognition (TSR) is a core perception capability for autonomous driving, where robustness to cross-region variation, long-tailed categories, and semantic ambiguity is essential for reliable real-world deployment. Despite steady progress in recognition accuracy, existing traffic sign datasets and benchmarks offer limited diagnostic insight into how different modeling paradigms behave under these practical challenges. We present TS-1M, a large-scale and globally diverse traffic sign dataset comprising over one million real-world images across 454 standardized categories, together with a diagnostic benchmark designed to analyze model capability boundaries. Beyond standard train-test evaluation, we provide a suite of challenge-oriented settings, including cross-region recognition, rare-class identification, low-clarity robustness, and semantic text understanding, enabling systematic and fine-grained assessment of modern TSR models. Using TS-1M, we conduct a unified benchmark across three representative learning paradigms: classical supervised models, self-supervised pretrained models, and multimodal vision-language models (VLMs). Our analysis reveals consistent paradigm-dependent behaviors, showing that semantic alignment is a key factor for cross-region generalization and rare-category recognition, while purely visual models remain sensitive to appearance shift and data imbalance. Finally, we validate the practical relevance of TS-1M through real-scene autonomous driving experiments, where traffic sign recognition is integrated with semantic reasoning and spatial localization to support map-level decision constraints. Overall, TS-1M establishes a reference-level diagnostic benchmark for TSR and provides principled insights into robust and semantic-aware traffic sign perception. Project page: https://guoyangzhao.github.io/projects/ts1m.

机器人研究所.title: Inertial Video World Models
机器人研究所.authors_text: Yuan Gao, Fan Xu, Yu Guo, Yuxu Lu, Zhengru Fang
机器人研究所.summary: InertialWorld introduces a novel video world model that incorporates inertia as a structural prior for improved autoregressive prediction, enhancing continuity and reducing error accumulation.
机器人研究所.debug_abstract: The physical world has inertia: it evolves from what already exists rather than being recreated at every instant. However, many existing video world models lack an explicit mechanism for inertial state evolution, leaving the continuity of motion and structure implicit in video prediction. During autoregressive rollouts, repeated reconstruction can accumulate errors and destabilize the predicted dynamics. To address this limitation, we introduce InertialWorld, an Inertial Video World Model that makes inertia a structural prior for autoregressive prediction: existing scene evidence is carried across time rather than reconstructed at every step. Central to this formulation is Inertial Memory, which turns memory from passive predictive context into an evolving video state with two complementary views: a dense Eulerian grid preserves scene-aligned evidence, while persistent Lagrangian carriers bind local content to learned canonical coordinates. At each step, the model transports the carrier content according to action-conditioned motion, predicts the complete next video state from the transported carriers and dense grid, and uses a learned gate to combine transported and newly predicted content into the memory for the next step. Extensive experiments across multiple domains, including robot manipulation, 3D game simulation, and open-world navigation, demonstrate that InertialWorld achieves competitive autoregressive prediction performance against strong video world model baselines. Codes link: https://github.com/YuanGao-YG/InertialWorld
